question.text: Vikram AIF Management charges a management fee and a performance fee as outlined in its IMA. Which of the following correctly describes the AIF's obligation regarding fee disclosure to investors?

answer.text: Fees need only be disclosed at the time of fund winding up
Fee details are confidential between the manager and trustee and cannot be shared with investors
Fees and expenses must be disclosed in the PPM/fund documents, in the Investor Charter, and through periodic reporting to investors as required under Regulation 22
Only the total expense ratio needs to be reported annually to SEBI, not to investors

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports fee and expense disclosure through several layers: the PPM and investment agreement set out the fee structure; recognised fund expenses include items such as valuation and reporting costs; the Investor Charter requires transparency on fees ascribed to the manager/sponsor and fees charged to the AIF or investee company; and Regulation 22 covers periodic reporting to investors. Fee confidentiality from investors and disclosing only at winding up would breach this layered transparency regime. The Trap: The 'only to SEBI' option is partially correct that the regulator receives information, but the obligation also runs directly to investors through the PPM, Investor Charter, and periodic reporting. Note: Replaced the keyed wording about IMA-specified frequency/format and a required NAV-impact fee report (not directly supported by the checked pages) with the source-backed PPM, Investor Charter, and Regulation 22 framing.
